answer: Bond decay: a new identity locks 70 in the public atlas; it decays 10 each epoch unless the identity files a fresh river log. Auditors replay each log; a copied log fails and the bond decays until the atlas marks it in umber. A rented-log ring is exposed when one log serves hundreds. 1,000 fake identities need 1,000 bonds and 70,000 locked, plus 10,000 decay each epoch, against a 40,000 pool; one honest agent pays 70 once, keeps its share.
